In [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]], the '''generalized multivariate log-gamma (G-MVLG) distribution''' is a [[multivariate distribution]] introduced by Demirhan and Hamurkaroglu<ref>{{cite journal|last=Demirhan|first=Haydar|author2=Hamurkaroglu, Canan|title=On a multivariate log-gamma distribution and the use of the distribution in the Bayesian analysis|journal=Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference|year=2011|volume=141|pages=1141–1152|doi=10.1016/j.jspi.2010.09.015|issue=3}}</ref> in 2011. The G-MVLG is a flexible distribution. [[Skewness]] and [[kurtosis]] are well controlled by the parameters of the distribution. This enables one to control [[statistical dispersion|dispersion]] of the distribution. Because of this property, the distribution is effectively used as a joint [[prior distribution]] in [[Bayesian analysis]], especially when the [[likelihood]] is not from the [[location-scale family]] of distributions such as [[normal distribution]].

==Joint probability density function==
If <math>\boldsymbol{Y} \sim
\mathrm{G}\text{-}\mathrm{MVLG}(\delta,\nu,\boldsymbol{\lambda},\boldsymbol{\mu})</math>, the joint [[probability density function]] (pdf) of <math>\boldsymbol{Y}=(Y_{1},\dots,Y_{k})</math> is given as the following:

:<math>f(y_1,\dots,y_k)= \delta^{\nu}\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(1-\delta)^{n}
\prod_{i=1}^k \mu_i \lambda_i^{-\nu-n}}{[\Gamma(\nu+n)]^{k-1}\Gamma(\nu)n!}
\exp\bigg\{(\nu +n)\sum_{i=1}^k \mu_i y_i - \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{\lambda_i}\exp\{\mu_i y_i\}\bigg\},</math>

where <math> \boldsymbol{y}\in \mathbb{R}^{k}, \nu>0, \lambda_{j}>0, \mu_{j}>0</math> for <math>j=1,\dots,k, \delta=\det(\boldsymbol{\Omega})^{\frac{1}{k-1}},</math> and

: <math>

\boldsymbol{\Omega}=\left(
\begin{array}{cccc}
  1 & \sqrt{\mathrm{abs}(\rho_{12})} & \cdots & \sqrt{\mathrm{abs}(\rho_{1k})} \\
  \sqrt{\mathrm{abs}(\rho_{12})} & 1 & \cdots & \sqrt{\mathrm{abs}(\rho_{2k})} \\
  \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
  \sqrt{\mathrm{abs}(\rho_{1k})} & \sqrt{\mathrm{abs}(\rho_{2k})} & \cdots & 1
\end{array}
\right), 
</math>

<math>\rho_{ij}</math> is the [[correlation]] between <math>Y_i</math> and <math>Y_j</math>, <math> \det(\cdot)</math> and <math>\mathrm{abs}(\cdot)</math> denote [[determinant]] and [[absolute value]] of inner expression, respectively, and <math>\boldsymbol{g}=(\delta,\nu,\boldsymbol{\lambda}^T,\boldsymbol{\mu}^T)</math> includes parameters of the distribution.

==Properties==
===Joint moment generating function===

The joint [[moment generating function]] of G-MVLG distribution is as the following:

:<math>M_{\boldsymbol{Y}}(\boldsymbol{t}) =\delta^\nu \bigg(\prod_{i=1}^k
\lambda_i^{t_i/\mu_i}\bigg)\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\Gamma(\nu +n)}{\Gamma(\nu)n!}
(1-\delta)^n \prod_{i=1}^k \frac{\Gamma(\nu+n+t_i/\mu_i)}{\Gamma(\nu+n)}.</math>

=== Marginal central moments ===
<math>r^\text{th}</math> marginal central moment of <math>Y_i</math> is as the following:

:<math>{\mu_i}'_r=\left[\frac{(\lambda_i/\delta)^{t_i/\mu_i}}{\Gamma(\nu)}\sum_{k=0}^r \binom{r}{k}\left[\frac{\ln(\lambda_i/\delta)}{\mu_i}\right]^{r-k}
\frac{\partial^k\Gamma(\nu+t_i/\mu_i)}{\partial t_i^k}\right]_{t_i=0}.</math>

===Marginal expected value and variance===
Marginal expected value <math>Y_i</math> is as the following:

:<math> \operatorname{E}(Y_{i})=\frac{1}{\mu_i}\big[\ln(\lambda_i/\delta)+\digamma(\nu)\big], </math>
:<math> \operatorname{var}(Z_i)=\digamma^{[1]}(\nu)/(\mu_i)^2</math>

where <math>\digamma(\nu)</math> and <math>\digamma^{[1]}(\nu)</math> are values of [[digamma function|digamma]] and [[trigamma function]]s at <math>\nu</math>, respectively.

==Related distributions==
Demirhan and Hamurkaroglu establish a relation between the G-MVLG distribution and the [[Gumbel distribution]] ([[type I extreme value distribution]]) and gives a multivariate form of the Gumbel distribution, namely the generalized multivariate Gumbel (G-MVGB) distribution. The joint probability density function of <math>\boldsymbol{T}\sim \mathrm{G}\text{-}\mathrm{MVGB}(\delta,\nu,\boldsymbol{\lambda},\boldsymbol{\mu})</math> is the following:

:<math>f(t_1,\dots,t_k; \delta,\nu,\boldsymbol{\lambda},\boldsymbol{\mu}))= \delta^\nu \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(1-\delta)^n
\prod_{i=1}^k \mu_i \lambda_i^{-\nu-n}}{[\Gamma(\nu+n)]^{k-1}\Gamma(\nu)n!}\exp\bigg\{-(\nu +n)\sum_{i=1}^k \mu_i t_i - \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{\lambda_i} \exp\{-\mu_i t_i\}\bigg\},\quad t_i\in \mathbb{R}.</math>

The Gumbel distribution has a broad range of applications in the field of [[risk analysis]]. Therefore, the G-MVGB distribution should be beneficial when it is applied to these types of problems.
